messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: P0 - GPU host node-rtx-23 is UNREACHABLE / kernel panic detected. Alert ID: PD-9482. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-9482

pagerduty-bot: Alert acknowledged by maya.sre (oncall). Escalation level: oncall -> infra-shift after 5m.

maya.sre: acked. I'm jumping on it. Observed: node-rtx-23 stopped heartbeating ~2m ago, kubelet NotReady.

zach.eng: saw a spike of 503s in the generation gateway tied to rtx-rack-1, likely that host. Pulling kubelet logs now.

maya.sre: logs (tail):
```
Mar 14 03:12:28 node-rtx-23 kernel: [  123.456789] NMI: kernel panic - not syncing: fatal exception
Mar 14 03:12:28 node-rtx-23 systemd: Kernel panic - not syncing
Mar 14 03:12:29 kubelet: node status changed to NotReady: NodeStatusUnknown
```

priya.platform: placing node-rtx-23 in cordon/drain? If it's kernel panic it's already down. We should trigger failover for affected pods.

maya.sre: cordoning now: `kubectl cordon node-rtx-23` -> `node/node-rtx-23 cordoned`. Draining: `kubectl drain node-rtx-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> some pods in `inference-prod` couldn't be gracefully evicted (stateful).

support-triage: Customer impact: Dashboard shows ~12% increase in 5xxs across /v1/generate for accounts hosted in eu-west-1; some customers reported degraded latency and OOM errors fallback. Not a full outage but degraded. Notified CS lead.

zach.eng: checking scheduler: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-rtx-23` -> shows 14 pods stuck. Kube-controller trying to reschedule but some replicas are anti-affinity pinned.

maya.sre: provisioning follow-up: scaling up spare pool in eu-west-1. Triggered autoscale group for dedicated-nodes to +3 GPUs (scaling request sent). ETA ~4m.

infra-shift: pinging colo ops to see if host has hardware console access. If kernel panic persisted, remote KVM reboot may be required. I've created ticket COLO-4123 and paged onsite tech.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation to infra-shift triggered (20:45 UTC).

priya.platform: temp routing: enabling fallback model variant on the gateway for customers hitting 503s to route to replica pool that doesn't require GPU. Rolling config via feature flag `fallback_cpu_variant=true` for 10% of traffic now.

maya.sre: quick mitigation notes: 1) cordoned node; 2) drained what we could; 3) scale-up in progress; 4) feature-flag fallback enabled. Monitoring error budget and SLOs.

zach.eng: log snippet from gateway around 03:13:10:
```
[03:13:10] ERROR request-id=abc123 upstream=503 host=node-rtx-23 connection reset by peer
[03:13:11] WARN request-id=def456 inference worker lost connection to GPU host
```

support-triage: CS update sent to top 3 affected customers with temporary mitigation steps.

maya.sre: infra-shift just reported remote KVM shows kernel oops, machine is unresponsive. They are attempting soft-reboot.

infra-shift: attempted soft powercycle via iLO -> host did not come back. KVM console shows machine halting at kernel oops loop. Recommending hard power cycle at rack. Onsite ETA ~12 minutes.

priya.platform: autoscale completed: new nodes came up and joined cluster (node-cpu-12, node-gpu-48), pods are rebalancing. Inference replica counts for critical services restored to target for most customers.

maya.sre: watching health: 5xx rate is trending down from 12% -> 2% in the last 6m after scale + fallback. Still seeing a couple of stuck stateful pods (model-cache) in CrashLoopBackOff that need manual recreate.

zach.eng: manual workaround for model-cache: created new PVC+pod on healthy node and primed cache with recent embeddings. Doing rolling delete on stuck pods.

infra-shift: onsite tech reports host power-cycled and node boots to grub then kernel panic again. Could be GPU driver/hw fault. Opening support case with OEM: OEM-CASE-8872.

maya.sre: given recurring kernel panic on boot, I'm marking node-rtx-23 as `unschedulable` permanently and initiating replacement workflow. We'll remove the host from autoscale pool and add new baremetal.

support-triage: Customer-facing status page updated: partial degradation in eu-west-1, mitigation in progress.

priya.platform: rolling back `fallback_cpu_variant` to 0 now that new capacity online. Monitoring for regression.

zach.eng: after manual recreate of model-cache, those pods stabilized. Error rates back to baseline (~0.3%). Latency minor bump for customers served by fallback during the window.

maya.sre: summary for handoff: root cause: node-rtx-23 kernel panic (suspected GPU driver/hardware). Impact: increased 5xxs and elevated latencies for subset of eu-west-1 traffic; partial customer degradation for ~18 minutes. Actions taken: cordon/drain, scale-up, fallback routing, manual pod recreate, OEM support engaged, host marked for replacement. Next oncall (priya.platform) will own replacement and OEM case updates.

priya.platform: taking over for post-incident. I'll confirm replacement schedule with colo and OEM. If anyone has additional notes, drop them here.

maya.sre: thanks all. I'll add a short incident note to the oncall log and tag for a 1-hour blameless postmortem tomorrow morning.

incident-bot: Incident PD-9482 marked resolved by maya.sre. Duration: 22m. Close reason: hardware kernel panic suspected; host replacement initiated.

support-triage: CS follow-ups queued; we offered credits to affected customers where SLA breached.

maya.sre: closing thread. Follow-up PR for runbook: add step to immediately enable CPU fallback when >5% 5xx sustained for 5m in region.

priya.platform: noted, will own runbook PR.
